content:
Today, Instapaper has released version 10 of its iPhone and iPad apps, bringing multiple improvements and a major redesign of its web platform. Here's the details.

"The biggest update to the iOS app in over a decade"

Instapaper announced today (via MacMagazine) updates to its iOS app, while adding new AI voice features to its Android app and giving its website a complete overhaul.

Instapaper 10 for iOS adds support for Liquid Glass and introduces four reading fonts:

Literata: a serif font designed by Google for Google Play Books. New York: a serif font designed by Apple for iOS. Open Sans: a sans-serif font commissioned by Google. Atkinson Hyperlegible: a sans-serif font developed by the Braille Institute.

This update also introduces Home Screen widgets, which Instapaper says can show what you're currently reading along with your recently saved items, and can be tapped to jump straight into reading.

For iPad users, Instapaper says this update improves multitasking; while iPhone and iPad users alike will notice more reliable background syncing, faster article downloads, and a redesigned onboarding tour.

Instapaper says today's update is the biggest in over a decade, and also includes:

Folder counts: All folders will now show how many articles or notes they contain. If folder counts stress you out more than they help, you can disable them under Settings > Behavior > Folder Counts. Folder sorting: Want to sort your folders or tags? Tap the "..." menu next to the folder title and choose your preferred sort order. Article list appearance: We've introduced a compact mode, along with new fonts and styles, and an easy way to customize the look of your article list. In the article list, tap "..." then tap "Appearance" to adjust style, font, and image thumbnails.

Finally, Instapaper has given its web platform a complete overhaul, adding features like a three-column reading mode and keyboard shortcuts, while the Android app now also supports AI voices.
